description: A grid sequencer of sixteen cells, each holding rhythmic subdivisions, where probability governs whether the cell fires and whether each subdivision inside it fires

params.text: Sets the global tempo, doubling for every step of the knob about 120 bpm at its default, and spanning 15 bpm to 960 bpm
Sets how many cells of the grid that sequence covers, 1 to 16
Picks how that sequence moves through the grid: the default path over its length, a random cell within its length, or a random walk between neighbouring cells
Sets the numerator of that sequence's ratio against the global tempo, 1 to 24
Sets the denominator of that sequence's ratio against the global tempo, 1 to 24
Sets the probability that this cell fires at all, 0 to 100%
Sets the probability that each subdivision inside this cell fires, 0 to 100%; when the cell fires and a subdivision does not, a single gate comes out instead
Sets the voltage this cell sends to its sequence's CV output, -10V to +10V
Returns all four sequences to the start of their paths
Turns that sequence on and off
Fills every cell with one of sixteen preset subdivision layouts, from quarter notes and triplets through to uniform random

inputs.text: An external clock, read either as a voltage setting the tempo or as pulses per quarter note, according to the External Clock Mode on the menu
A trigger returns all four sequences to the start of their paths

outputs.text: Fires a pulse for each subdivision of that sequence's current cell that wins its probability roll
Carries the voltage set by that sequence's current cell

notes: click a cell to add subdivisions, Shift-click to double them up to sixteen, drag within a cell to change them, and Ctrl-click a subdivision to switch it off or on
the sequencer is stopped when the module is added, so nothing fires until the run button is pressed.
menu: Gate mode — Gates, which last the subdivision, or Triggers
CV mode — Independent changes the voltage at every cell, Sample and Hold changes it only when the cell was triggered
Volt Range — the span of the cell voltages: +1V, +2V, plus or minus 5V, or +10V
Mouse Drag — horizontal or vertical, which way a drag inside a cell changes its subdivisions
External Clock Mode — how the EXT jack is read: CV (0V = 120 bpm), or 2 PPQN, 4 PPQN, 8 PPQN, 12 PPQN or 24 PPQN pulses per quarter note
Ext Clk Auto Start — in the pulse modes the clock starts when pulses arrive and stops when they stop
Display — blooms or circles, which changes the drawing and nothing else
